pages.title: Architecture Overview: Kernel, Gatekeepers, and the Worker Topology
pages.purpose: The big-picture system design: the workshop-backend as kernel, User/Overseer/AdminSettings/PendingLogin Durable Objects, gadget facets in dynamic workers, the router as public origin, gatekeepers as separate workers, and which package owns which responsibility.
instructions: Explain the DO topology: which DOs exist, how they are reached (ctx.exports, idFromName(email), newUniqueId), and what each owns
Explain the router's binding-scan routing for GATEKEEPER_* services and the /api path
State the ownership boundaries enforced by AGENTS.md (kernel held to a higher review bar)

pages.title: Persistence: DO Storage, KV, R2, and the Git Object Store
pages.purpose: Where data lives: typed-storage collections in each DO, the workspace's real git loose-object store, KV namespaces (BLUEPRINTS, AVATARS, admin config mirror), R2 (BLUEPRINT_CONTENT), and the schema-version/migration approach.
instructions: Cover the read-only legacy collections (code, snapshots, chatDraftUpdates) and the git migration
Explain makeOverseerStorage singletons/collections and the schema version 0-3 migration ladder
Explain why git-store deliberately has no ref layer and where refs live instead

pages.title: The Cap'n Web RPC API Contract
pages.purpose: How the SPA, backend, and gatekeepers communicate: the PublicApi/AuthenticatedApi/Overseer/GadgetClient/GatekeeperClient capability chain, WebSocket transport, @validateRpc, promise pipelining, stub disposal, coded errors, and subscription patterns.
instructions: Cover the coded-error families (OPEN_GADGET_ERROR_CODES, AUTH_ERROR_CODES) and why messages double as fallback classification
Document the project RPC conventions from AGENTS.md: @validateRpc, pipelining, no stubs in useState, Symbol.dispose
Trace the capability chain from PublicApi to AuthenticatedApi to Overseer to GadgetClient

pages.title: Blueprints and Output Formats
pages.purpose: Blueprint creation/update, the three-store propagation (Gadget DO -> User DO -> KV) plus R2 content, the .gadget archive format, featured blueprints, bundled format blueprints and output presentation, and the two instantiation paths (user landing page, agent createGadget).
instructions: Cover binding assignments at instantiation (two-phase creation including agent spawners) in newGadgetFromBlueprint
Document the dirty-flag retry and orphaned-blueprint lifecycle
Explain format-blueprints: stable IDs, sidecar output, AdminSettings install on first /api request, promote-once

pages.title: Build System, Dev Tooling, and the Release Pipeline
pages.purpose: The developer toolchain: Vite+ tasks and caching rules (env declaration, cache:false cases, build:app shape), run-dev-server internals, the configurator build, and scripts/release (build/upload/promote, manifest contract, candidates, deploy-inputs).
instructions: Cover the deploy-wizard input conventions (deploy-inputs.json, NO_DEFAULT_CRED_INPUTS)
Document the release pipeline stages and the manifest placeholder scheme ($ACCOUNT_ID, $SECRET, ...)
Summarize the vp caching pitfalls from AGENTS.md only as they affect someone changing the build (env stripping, read-write paths, singleThreaded rationale)

pages.title: Change Guides: Representative Maintenance Tasks
pages.purpose: Focused, source-grounded walkthroughs of representative changes: adding a gatekeeper binding-wise, changing the shared RPC API safely, extending AdminConfig, adding an agent tool, and changing the gadget sandbox environment.
instructions: Each guide must trace the concrete files to touch and the invariants to preserve (doc-comment every exported workshop-shared member, validateBindingName chokepoints, capnweb-validate, no parallel mechanisms)
Explicitly mark anything the repository does not establish as uncertain
Ground every step in existing code that demonstrates the pattern (e.g. an existing gatekeeper, an existing tool)

pages.title: Testing: Unit, Workerd, and Integration Harness
pages.purpose: How tests are organized and run: the shared vitest task conventions, workerd-pool suites and the assert-workerd guard, the integration-tests harness (createTestHarness, NetworkInterceptor, rpc-client), the fixture gatekeeper, and the release-manifest golden test.
instructions: Cover the fixture gatekeeper's two deliberate departures and the afterAll escape assertion
Document why fake timers cannot work in integration tests and the no-clean-slate rules
Explain the test:run vs cached test distinction and the with-timeout watchdog

pages.title: Gatekeeper Architecture: Vendors, Accounts, Sessions
pages.purpose: The gatekeeper contract every connector implements: GatekeeperVendor/GatekeeperUser/Gatekeeper DO surfaces, connect flows and incremental scopes, sessions/resources/capabilities, ambient auto-provisioning and the provisioning policy, loopback entrypoints the overseer provides, hooks, and slash commands.
instructions: Cover the ambient/autoprovisioned model (singleton, providesUi, named chat bindings, modes disabled/optional/enabled)
Document the loopback entrypoints (GatekeeperLoopback, GatekeeperHookLoopback, AgentSelfLoopback, CodeModeTailLoopback, GadgetTailLoopback) and what they exist for
Trace the lifecycle: connectAccount -> GatekeeperUser account -> getGatekeeperClassFor -> gatekeeper facet per workpiece -> session capabilities

pages.title: Shipped Gatekeepers: Package Catalog
pages.purpose: A grounded tour of each packages/gatekeeper-* implementation: what it connects to, its account model (OAuth vs auto-provisioned), distinctive internals (e.g. cloudflare's observability defence layers, mcp-shared trust tiers, context's three DOs), and its observer strategy.
instructions: Cover the cloudflare gatekeeper's three unrelated purposes (sign-in, billing, telemetry) from its README/source
Explain mcp-shared as a shared library behind gatekeeper-mcp and gatekeeper-mcp-portal, and the tools.ts trust boundary
Prefer structure and contract over exhaustive feature lists; cite each package's entrypoint and key modules
State observer strategies only where the repository establishes them (docs/observers.md decision table); mark uncertainty otherwise

pages.title: Deployment Administration and Configuration
pages.purpose: The AdminSettings DO, AdminConfig shape and KV mirror, the AdminApi capability (isAdmin minted once), the admin-panel conventions (opt-out defaults, ambient modes, formats curation), feature flags, and deployment env vars; distinguishes soft config from env-driven auth.
instructions: Document the enabled-by-default opt-out convention and the three-state ambient gatekeeper modes
Explain the single reserved KV key mirror (.adminConfig) and why only the DO writes it
List the deployment env vars actually read by workshop-backend (ADMINS, DEPLOY_URL, PUBLIC_BASE_URL, limits flags) with citations

pages.title: AI Models and AI Gateway Billing
pages.purpose: How AI models are configured and billed: LanguageModelGatekeeper, user model configs, AI Gateway routing and cost logs, the optional free-tier/credits flow (checkUsageAndBalance), and every relevant env var.
instructions: Document where model credentials live (User DO model configs / LanguageModelGatekeeper) and that models are workspace-independent
Explain the WORKERS_AI binding transport vs API token transport and the CF_AI_GATEWAY_USE_BINDING caveat
Trace checkUsageAndBalance decision table (connected + balance >= $2 -> BYOK, else free tier, else blocked)

pages.title: Observability: Logging, Error Reporting, Analytics
pages.purpose: The server-side logger and its field vocabulary, observability context, backend issue reporting, the frontend error-reporting pipeline (opt-in, POST /api/client-errors, gatekeeper postMessage frames), DO telemetry/retry wrappers, and product analytics events.
instructions: Cover retryOnDoReset and wrapDoStubForTelemetry semantics
Document the createLogger conventions from AGENTS.md (component/vendorId fields, event names, no secrets)
Explain the frontend contract: VITE_FRONTEND_ERROR_REPORTING gating, unverified reportedUserId, normalized pageLocation

pages.title: Sharing: Permission Graph and Lazy Revocation
pages.purpose: How gadgets are shared: collaborators and roles (build/use), the permission graph of user/share-link edges, the fixed-point effective-role algorithm, share-key HMAC storage, lazy revocation, keepUsers re-rooting, and session restart on revocation.
instructions: Cover share link key minting (HMAC-SHA-256 of a random key) and the link-as-first-key storage shape
Document resource isolation between collaborators (BYO accounts/models baked into bindings) and ctx.abort() session termination
Explain the computeEffectiveRoles fixed-point algorithm and why effective role is never denormalized

pages.title: Observers: Read-Through Sharing Permissions
pages.purpose: The observer enforcement mechanism: ObserverRecord storage, ensureObserver at open() with the ObserverConfigCallback modal, getVerifier/addObserver verification, forward exclusion via excludeObservers, and the per-gatekeeper strategy taxonomy.
instructions: Cover prohibitAllSharing as the blunt stopgap vs per-observer excludeObservers
Explain the verifier pattern (opaque observerId, verifier minted by the observer's own account, vendor-mismatch throws)
Note that docs/observers.md is a historical plan and verify claims against current source

pages.title: Actions, Approval Queue, and Auto-Approval
pages.purpose: The human-in-the-loop pipeline: ActionRecord lifecycle, the ApprovalQueue/ObservationAuthorizer contract, simulated outcomes that let agents continue, the action log and pagination, and the auto-approval drainer.
instructions: Cover the three action-collection indexes and the auto-approval drain's single-flight guard
Explain the simulation model described in README and how observations differ from actions
Trace submitAction from gatekeeper to ActionRecord to approve/reject and applyAction

pages.title: The AI Agent: Loop, Tools, Chat Log, and Resumption

pages.title: Authentication and the User Model

pages.title: The Gadget Sandbox: Dynamic Workers and the Client Iframe

Document the worker-def fields: globalOutbound: null, compatibility flags, env built by getEnvForLoader, GadgetTailLoopback tails
Explain restore()/persistent stubs, the restore-forger, and why executed code (not gadget workers) gets that capability

pages.title: The Workspace Overseer: Workpieces, Code, and Chats
